text:
QUESTIONS, aimed at the weakest links first. Ask only questions whose answer would change how the idea is built, and say which two build choices each one decides:

Q1: Do the baseline's saved `model.pt` files already hold the answer, so no new training is needed? | decides: read gains from the existing baseline checkpoints vs spend 3 new full baseline runs on measurement
A1: Unknown whether the harness kept them. If it did, `state_dict` holds `blocks.{i}.n1.weight`, `n2.weight`, `attn.latent_norm.weight`, `attn.q_norm.weight`, `attn.k_norm.weight` and `norm.weight` for every seed. Reading them costs nothing and fully settles mean and CV at the full budget. Nothing in the material above contains these numbers.

Q2: How much CV does a gain vector reach from gradient noise alone under this optimizer? | decides: the idea's "within 10% of uniform means idle" threshold vs a threshold calibrated against the noise floor (about 0.2)
A2: The gains sit in AdamW with lr 3e-3 and eps 1e-10. With eps that small, Adam is nearly sign-normalized, so even a channel with a tiny, signal-free gradient moves at the full rate. The random-walk displacement is about 3e-3·√(Σ mult²) = 3e-3·√1200.7 ≈ 0.104 at the full budget, or about 0.09 after decay shrinks the early steps. Pure noise therefore gives a CV of about 0.10–0.13. The 10% test threshold sits at or below the noise floor and cannot tell an idle gain from a used one.

Q3: How far does weight decay alone move the mean? | decides: put the scalars in the decayed AdamW "other" group vs add a no-decay group in `build_optimizers`
A3: The norms are 1-D, so they land in AdamW with weight_decay 0.1. The schedule gives 15.5 + 1037 + 229.5 = 1282 effective full-lr steps. With no gradient, the factor is exp(−3e-4·1282) = 0.681, and it is 0.864 by step 500. Decay is real, but it is weak next to Adam's step size. Equilibrium only needs the gradient signal-to-noise ratio m/√v ≥ 0.1·w, which a scalar (a sum over channels) meets far more easily than a single channel.

Q4: Which gain vectors are functionally redundant, and which are not? | decides: the 25-scalar set (n1, n2, final) vs the 61-scalar set (every RMSNorm instance)
A4: The n1, n2 and latent_norm gains feed straight into Linear layers (wq/compress/rotary, w_gate/w_up, expand). Their per-channel values are exactly absorbable as column scales of those matrices, so they matter only for optimization: they give Adam a diagonal preconditioner that Muon's orthogonalized updates cannot produce. The q_norm/k_norm gains, and the final gain under tied embeddings, are not absorbable. They set the logit geometry directly.

Q5: Where must the "1.4x attention temperature" scalar sit to actually reach q·k? | decides: scalar on q_norm (content temperature) vs scalar on n1 (rotary temperature only)
A5: The overall scale of n1 cancels in qc (q_norm), k (k_norm) and v (latent_norm). It survives only in qr and kr, both of which come from n1, so an n1 scalar s scales the rotary logits by s² and leaves the content logits untouched. A 1.4x content temperature therefore needs a scalar on q_norm (or k_norm). q_norm is outside the 9,600-parameter set the idea names, so the 25-scalar build cannot deliver L2.

Q6: Which statistic of the q/k gains is meaningful? | decides: one temperature scalar on q only vs a scalar on both q and k
A6: The content logit depends only on the per-channel product gq⊙gk. Each 64-vector is shared across all 6 heads of its layer, because RMSNorm(64) acts on the last dimension. The individual vectors can drift along gq·gk = const, with decay pulling them toward gq = gk. The CV of each vector alone is therefore ambiguous: measure the CV and mean of the product. One scalar on q captures the whole temperature; a second scalar on k is a redundant direction.

Q7: Does a 500-step probe predict the full-budget end state? | decides: a 500-step baseline probe vs a full 1,525-step probe
A7: No. At step 500 the noise CV is about 0.066 and the decay factor 0.864. At the end they are about 0.10 and 0.681. Any real per-channel drift also keeps growing during the 1,037 flat steps. A 500-step measurement underestimates both mean drift and CV, so the open question requires the full budget, or Q1's checkpoints.

Q8: How do you tell feature selection from temperature in the end state, beyond CV? | decides: convert the final norm to a scalar vs keep the final gain vector
A8: Count the channels with |g| < 0.2·mean and check for sign flips, since Adam can push a gain negative. Then mean-ablate each vector in the checkpoint (replace it by its mean) and measure the loss change on train-shard windows split by token-frequency bucket. Never use val. For the absorbable gains (n1/n2/latent), ablation overstates their importance because the downstream matrices co-adapted. For the final and q/k gains, the ablation delta is the direct answer.

Q9: What should the scalars be initialized to? | decides: init 1.0 (the current start) vs init to the baseline's end-of-run mean
A9: Unknown until Q1 or the probe is answered. Initializing at 1.0 keeps step-0 behavior identical to the baseline, so it preserves the paired comparison. Initializing at the end-state mean (if it differs from 1 by more than 0.2) removes a drift the scalar would otherwise spend early steps on. Either way, `torch.tensor(value)` draws no RNG.

Q10: Muon decays matrices hard. Do the gains carry the scales Muon cannot hold? | decides: a plain scalar vs a Gemma-style (1+w) vector that decays toward identity
A10: Muon's decay alone would give exp(−0.02·0.1·1282) = exp(−2.56) ≈ 0.077, so Muon matrix scale sits at an lr/wd equilibrium that ignores the gradient. That leaves the n2 gain as the free knob for the gate pre-activation scale, and the q/k gains as the only knob for content temperature. This supports the idea's premise that the temperatures matter. It also predicts that baseline n2 and q/k means drift away from 1, a belief not yet measured.

KNOWN:
- The norm gains (n1, n2, latent_norm, q_norm, k_norm, final) are 1-D, so they go to AdamW with lr 3e-3, betas (0.9, 0.95), eps 1e-10 and weight_decay 0.1. No norm is exempt from decay. [script]
- Effective full-lr steps over the run: warmup 15.5, flat 1,037, cooldown 229.5, total 1,282. Σ mult² ≈ 1,200.7. [script]
- With no gradient, decay leaves a gain at 0.681 at the end and 0.864 at step 500. [belief, derived from the script]
- The noise-floor displacement per channel is about 0.10 at the end and about 0.066 at step 500. A pure-noise CV of about 0.10–0.13 means the "<10% means idle" test cannot discriminate. [belief]
- Adam's eps is 1e-10, so updates are nearly scale-invariant. The global grad clip at 1.0 does not throttle the gain updates. [script + belief]
- The `RMSNorm` class is shared by all 61 instances. Editing the class converts all of them (−12,611 params). The 25-scalar set (−9,575) needs a separate class or a flag. The stated −9,560 matches neither. [script]
- The q_norm and k_norm gains (64 each) are shared across the 6 heads and touch only the 64 content dims. The 32 rotary dims are never normalized. [script]
- An n1 scalar s scales only the rotary logits, by s². The content temperature lives only in gq⊙gk. [script]
- The n1, n2 and latent gains are exactly absorbable into the columns of the following Linear layers. The q/k and final gains are not, the final one because of the tied head. [script]
- Muon's decay factor under its own lr and wd would be about 0.077 over the run, so matrix scales are set by equilibrium. [belief, derived from the script]
- The baseline end-state gain mean and CV are not measured anywhere in the material provided. [measured: absent]
- Scalar parameters made with `torch.tensor(...)` draw no RNG, so paired-seed init alignment holds. [script]
- The `state_dict` keys change, but the exam builds `GPT(cfg)` from this script, so loading stays consistent. [belief]
- Gemma's (1+w) gain makes decay pull toward identity: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/gemma/modeling_gemma.py [web]
- modded-nanogpt uses weightless rms_norm: https://github.com/kellerjordan/modded-nanogpt [web]

ASSUMES:
- A learned scale is needed at every norm, not a fixed constant.
- The useful content of a gain vector is its mean, and per-channel spread is noise or decay damage.
- One scalar per norm suffices for attention, rather than one per head.
- The scalars should share the decayed AdamW group (unless a no-decay group is added).
- The tied head does not need any per-channel decoupling from the input embedding.
- The baseline gains drift toward zero under decay rather than being held up by gradient.
- 1.4x is the right starting content temperature at a 1/√96 SDPA scale.

NEW IDEAS:

SLOT: drop
IDEA: Identity-anchored gains (1+w)
MECHANISM: Drop the assumption "the scalars share the decayed group with a target of 0". Keep the per-channel vectors but parameterize them as 1+w, so AdamW's decay pulls toward identity instead of toward 0.68x shrinkage.
PREDICTION: End-state gain mean near 1 with CV near the noise floor, and loss equal to or slightly better than baseline. Parameter count unchanged.
TEST: A 500-step paired run. Compare the gain mean (baseline expected below 0.9 from decay) and the matched loss.
SOURCE: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/gemma/modeling_gemma.py
PART: State across depth: normalization placement and initialization
KIND: port

SLOT: strengthen
IDEA: Per-head log-temperature on q
MECHANISM: Replace the q_norm gain with 6 per-head scalars stored as log τ, exempt from decay, initialized to log 1.4. Multiplicative Adam steps let each head set its own sharpness.
PREDICTION: Head temperatures spread out by step 500 (some above 2, some below 1). Attention entropy falls in layers 3–11.
TEST: A 300-step run logging the 72 temperatures. If all stay within ±10% of 1.4, the per-head freedom is unused.
SOURCE: own
PART: State across depth: normalization placement and initialization
KIND: port

SLOT: specialise
IDEA: Collapse gains to their mean at cooldown start
MECHANISM: At step 1,067, overwrite every gain vector with its mean and freeze the spread (keep only a scalar from then on). This tests whether the accumulated per-channel spread carries information in the late phase.
PREDICTION: If the spread is noise, there is no loss jump at step 1,068 and the final val is equal or better. If it encodes features, the loss jumps and does not recover.
TEST: Paired seeds. Compare step 1,068–1,080 train loss with baseline.
SOURCE: own
PART: State across depth: normalization placement and initialization
KIND: leap
BREAKS: Gains learned throughout keep their per-channel spread to the end.
KILL: Mean train loss over steps 1,068–1,080 more than 0.02 above paired baseline.

SLOT: port
IDEA: Input-embedding scalar to fix the tiny layer-0 stream
MECHANISM: Put one learned scalar (no decay, init about 10) on the token embedding before it is expanded into the 4 streams, so the raw stream RMS is not about 0.02 against a 1.4–10.9 residual.
PREDICTION: The layer-0 attention gradient falls from 0.24 toward the 0.02–0.03 band, and early loss improves.
TEST: A 45-step smoke logging per-layer attention gradient norms.
SOURCE: own
PART: Residual streams: embedding input and stream initialization
KIND: port

SLOT: combine
IDEA: Scalar temperatures with nGPT's scale reparameterization
MECHANISM: Store each scalar as p with effective value p·(s_init/s_scale), as nGPT does for its scaling factors. This sets Adam's effective step on the temperature independently of the global lr_adam.
PREDICTION: Temperatures move about 3x slower or faster as chosen. Removes early overshoot of the 1.4x q-scale during warmup.
TEST: A 100-step run comparing the scalar trajectories and attention max-logit with the plain-scalar build.

LINK STATUS:
- L1: open | Not built. The stated −9,560 matches neither −9,575 (25 scalars) nor −12,611 (61). It also conflicts with L2, which needs q_norm in the set.
- L2: open | Unmeasured. If the scalar goes on n1 rather than q_norm, it scales only the rotary logits by s², so the breaks_if would fire from a build error, not a refutation.
- L3: open | No checkpoint data. Mean-ablating the baseline final gain on train-shard frequency buckets would answer it cheaply.
- L4: open | The baseline CV and mean are still unmeasured. Now known: pure decay gives 0.681 and the noise CV is about 0.10–0.13, so "expect CV < 0.15" sits on the noise floor. The CV > 0.25 break condition is a fair discriminator.
- L5: open | The quantity field is malformed and nothing was measured.
- L6: open | No seeds run, and the pooled exam baseline mean is not given.
